text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate on inference fleet (us-west1). 95th latency spike + growing CUDA OOM count across gpu-pool-nodes. Alert: serving-runtime.errors > 5% over 2m. Paging on-call.

ash (sre): I'm on it. seeing autoscaler logs show a ton of scale-from-0 -> 8 -> 1 within minutes. looks like repeated rapid scale ups then snapbacks.

mike (ml-oncall): Logs show model v3.1B processes hitting CUDA OOM in the pod stderr. frequent restart loops after node attach. sample from pod: 
```
[2026-03-15T15:12:02Z] RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 15.75 GiB total, 14.1 GiB already allocated)
Traceback ...
```

carla (eng-runtime): autoscaler is responding to a short traffic spike, spinning up a bunch of pods. those pods initialize KV cache and hit a big memory allocation at startup. with many pods starting simultaneously we oversubscribe GPUs and OOM.

jess (infra): Node churn is also real — nodes get provisioned then quickly drained by kube-proxy evictions when pods crash -> CA sees capacity drop -> scale again. cycle keeps repeating.

ash (sre): customer impact: internal metrics show 18% of requests in us-west1 getting 5xx or timeouts last 5m. product-custops tagged. dmitri, can you confirm if any customer-facing incidents reported?

dmitri (product-custops): already got 2 support pings about increased errors for async embeddings. customers on dedicated pools might be fine; this looks host-level for shared hosted API. raising banner now.

ash (sre): immediate mitigation plan (short list):
1) pause cluster autoscaler (prevent further thrash)
2) reduce deployment.maxSurge / set HPA max replicas to a conservative value
3) roll out a sequential restart (one pod at a time) to let KV caches warm gradually
4) temporary traffic steering to eu-west1 spare capacity if healthy

mike (ml-oncall): agree. also suggest switching the model instance to lower-init-memory config (reduced kv cache) or use quantized variant for warm restarts. I'll prepare a model-variant flag for fast switch.

carla (eng-runtime): i'm running commands now. pausing CA: 
```bash
kubectl -n infra annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler "cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/paused=true" --overwrite
```
Done — autoscaler pause annotated.

jess (infra): limiting HPA: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch hpa inference-deploy --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/maxReplicas","value":6}]'
```
Patched to maxReplicas=6.

ash (sre): setting rollout strategy to maxUnavailable=1 and maxSurge=0 for the inference deployment to force serial restarts.

carla (eng-runtime): applied. Deployment spec updated: 
```yaml
strategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
  rollingUpdate:
    maxUnavailable: 1
    maxSurge: 0
```

mike (ml-oncall): model toggle ready. switching 10% of traffic to quantized-v3 now for canary. if stable, we can expand.

ash (sre): starting sequential restart of pods (one-by-one): 
```bash
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl -n inference delete {}
```
Doing one at a time with a 30s gap.

jess (infra): I also cordoned the most unstable nodes to stop new pod scheduling: `kubectl cordon gpunode-54` and `kubectl cordon gpunode-61`.

dmitri (product-custops): banner posted: "Partial degradation in us-west1 for hosted inference; working on mitigation. Temporary traffic re-routed where possible." customers notified.

ash (sre): monitoring OOM count after restarts... initial pods coming up slow and staying up. OOM rate dropped from 7% -> 1.2% in last 4m. good sign.

carla (eng-runtime): confirmed the sequential restarts avoided the simultaneous heavy allocations. the KV cache fill is now staggered.

mike (ml-oncall): quantized canary looks stable for 12 minutes. tail latency slightly better. would recommend keeping canary at 25% while we stabilize.

jess (infra): autoscaler remains paused. recommend we keep CA off until we adjust scale-from-0 thresholds and set cooldown to avoid oscillation.

ash (sre): follow-on actions (tickets):
- tune CA scaling cooldown + scale-down delay (infra)
- add startup memory limit guard in runtime to avoid large contiguous allocations (eng-runtime)
- add a soft-start mode for KV cache (ml)
- write a runbook step to set HPA caps during rush windows (sre)

carla (eng-runtime): logging a PR to add staged KV warm start + fallback to disk-backed cache if memory constrained. cc @mike for validation.

mike (ml-oncall): will validate. also adding unit to the model packaging to allow booting with smaller kv_window param.

dmitri (product-custops): customers want ETA. recommend "partial mitigation in 20–30m, full stabilization after configuration tweaks and CA re-enable". posting update in support thread.

ash (sre): marking incident status: mitigated (partial). keeping channel open for follow-ups. If OOMs reappear we escalate to SEV2.

carla (eng-runtime): note for postmortem: root cause = autoscaler responding to microbursts which caused simultaneous cold-start memory pressure on GPU hosts -> oversubscription -> OOM -> crashloops -> autoscaler-triggered snapback -> further instability.

ash (sre): thanks all. handoff to on-call for next hour: @mike please monitor metrics and I'll update the postmortem ticket.

mike (ml-oncall): ack. I'll watch OOMs, latency, and CA logs. will reopen channel if needed. :thumbsup:
